text: Psychometric evaluation of the BDI-II (Beck, Steer, & Brown, 1996) examined internal consistency, factorial validity, and gender differences; both BDI and BDI-II showed high internal reliability in the full student sample, but significant mean-score differences required new analogue-research cutoffs. Exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses favored a 2-factor solution for both inventories, accounting for 41% (BDI) and 46% (BDI-II) of common variance; solutions cross-validated reliably, though factor importance varied by gender. The BDI-II has the stronger factor structure. Separately, a diffusion MRI technique yielded orientationally invariant axon diameter and density indices using a four-compartment tissue model with optimized multishell high-angular-resolution pulsed-gradient-spin-echo acquisition, tested in simulation and on fixed monkey (preclinical) and live human brains (clinical 3T, ~1 hour). It distinguished natural axon diameter distributions, correlating well for monkeys but weaker for humans; corpus callosum and corticospinal tract maps matched histology trends.
